title: The keyboard reaches the card menu, pin and collapse controls
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a dispatcher whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > on the Work Orders card, View and Create & Edit are both ticked. The Admin role has both).
  2. In the top bar, choose the location you test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  3. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (the display switcher only shows at 1024 px and wider).
  4. The location has these eligible technicians (examples): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo".
    • A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > open the staff member > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, the Time Clock (clockable) setting is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location.
    • To add one: Settings > Staff > add a staff member with those settings (e.g. first name "ZZAUTOTEST Ana", last name "Alpha").
  5. How to create each work order below:
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the customer (add it from the window if it does not exist, e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Co") and any asset > Create.
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician to the technician named (leave it empty for an unassigned one).
    • Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate; approve the estimate for Approved; use the status control on the work order page for In Progress, Review (Ready for Review) and Complete; decline the estimate for Declined; Finance tab > Create Invoice for Invoiced; record a payment for the full amount for Paid. Set the lead technician before invoicing.
    • Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801).
  6. Work orders (Approved): lead Ana — "ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Co"; lead Ben — "ZZAUTOTEST Charlie Co"; no lead — "ZZAUTOTEST Golf Co".
  7. Put the mouse aside. From step 4 on, use only the keyboard.
  8. The keyboard and focus design is not finished yet (the design shows no keyboard behaviour). Where a step names a key, try Tab, Shift+Tab, the arrow keys, Enter, Space and Escape, and write down which key does what.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST" in Search so only your test work orders show.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (the design tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Using only the keyboard, focus the Alpha Co card and move focus to its more-actions button.
  5. Press Enter to open the menu, then press Escape.
  6. Move focus to the pin button in Ana's column header and press Enter, then press Enter again.
  7. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (the design tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  8. Move focus to the collapse button of Ana's group and press Enter, then press Enter again.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: the more-actions button appears when the card has keyboard focus (not only on mouse hover).
  • Step 5: Enter (or Space) opens the menu and Escape closes it.
  • Step 6: Ana is pinned, then unpinned, using only the keyboard.
  • Step 8: Ana's group collapses, then expands, using only the keyboard.
  • Engineering is building these now. The exact keys are not designed yet: write down the keys that worked.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10054 (Story 11, Keyboard access and focus); SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S11-R2, S11-R5, S11-R7, S11-R8, S3-R13, read 8 Oct 2026. Review Decisions page 853901313, SQ-15 (Open) and UX-19 (Open). Inline PRD comment by Slavcho Mitrov, 28 Sep 2026, lists what is still open with design. Tech plan (revised 24 Sep 2026) Phase 11.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-R2: “Design must define keyboard access to the more-actions menu.”
  • S11-R5: “Design must define how Escape cancels an interaction.”
  • S11-R7: “Design must define keyboard access to pin and unpin.”
  • S11-R8: “Design must define keyboard access to group collapse and expand.”
  • S3-R13: “Reveal the card’s more-actions overlay on hover or keyboard focus.”
  • Tech plan Phase 11 controls: “Every control is a real button with an `aria-label`; the more-actions overlay reveals on `:focus-within`; pin and collapse are keyboard-reachable (S11-R2, S11-R7, S11-R8)”
  • Tech plan Phase 11 tests menu: “more-actions opens with Enter and Space; the overlay is visible on focus”
